outcome: Vital signs (average arterial pressure, systolic pressure)
cohort: The study included 480 lying-in women undergoing caesarean section, divided equally into an experiment group and a control group.
finding: Ropivacaine resulted in elevated arterial and systolic pressures at 5 and 10 minutes post-CSEA, extended onset time, shorter duration of sensory and motor block, and a significantly lower incidence of adverse reactions compared to bupivacaine.
mod_finding: The study found that ropivacaine is more recommended for anesthesia during caesarean section due to less influence on hemodynamics, shorter block duration, and fewer adverse reactions, which aid patient recovery.
followup_time: Observations were taken at 5 min and 10 min after combined spinal and epidural analgesia (CSEA) and 'during anesthesia'.
